# Playtest round 7: triage

Generated by `node scripts/playtest-registry.mjs report 7` from playtests/REGISTRY.jsonl and the round's friction JSONL. Do not edit by hand; re-run it.

113 friction rows this round (39 of them praise, counted and not triaged); 74 linked to 46 issues (27 new, 19 repeats); 0 not yet linked.

By tier: 14 A, 3 B, 29 C.

Suggested A/B/C is the registry's guess from the kind (A: build it, B: a deviation for the sponsor, C: leave it as the original). **Norm confirms each one** (`confirm <id> A|B|C`) after checking it against the ZIL and the oracle.

## New issues

| Issue | Title | Area / room | Kind | Rows this round | Rows in all | Rounds | Suggested | Norm confirms | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SF-151 | Click menus: Examine on "robot in the third bin" sends "examine floyd", so the game's refusal ("You don't see anyone by that name here.") spoils the reveal | Click menus / Robot Pool | bug | 2 | 2 | 7 | A | A | fixed | Interface. FLOYD-F refuses the word FLOYD until his TOUCHBIT is set (ship.zil 448-451). The oracle (seed 1: STARBOARD, FORE, EXAMINE FLOYD) gives the same refusal, so the words are canon, but no player could type the name yet. Our menu chose them: nounCandidates (engine/zmenus.js:63-91) puts the name's noun "floyd" first. Checked at HEAD: objectOffers(FLOYD) sends "examine floyd". The oracle's EXAMINE THIRD ROBOT gives "You can't see the robot in the third bin very well..." and the reveal. Fix: until FLOYD has TOUCHBIT, drop FLOYD from his noun candidates (THIRD ROBOT resolves; ship.zil 283-284), in every entry that names him. The SF-086 label is not the fault. Rows: r7-click-fullA#1, r7-click-fullB#1. |
| SF-152 | Click menus: Close is offered on things whose routine only refuses it (the jammer: "Huh?"; the simulation booth: "The booth has no door.") | Click menus / Storage | bug | 3 | 3 | 7 | A | A | fixed | Interface. JAMMER-F answers OPEN and CLOSE with HUH (station.zil 115-116). The jammer has OPENBIT (station.zil 90), so answeredVerbs (engine/zmenus.js:391) offers Close. SIMULATION-BOOTH-F answers both with "The booth has no door." (village.zil 188-189). Oracle, route step 229 + CLOSE JAMMER and OPEN JAMMER: "Huh?" both times. The replies stay canon; the entries are ours, as with SF-011 (the counter) and SF-126 (Wear on worn boots). Fix: declare OPEN and CLOSE hidden for JAMMER (rules/level5.js menus) and for SIMULATION-BOOTH-F (its village rules module). Rows: r7-click-fullA#10, #22, r7-click-fullB#26. |
| SF-153 | Click menus: "Reach in" is never offered, though DISPENSER-HOLE-F answers it ("You can just feel something with your fingertips") | Click menus / The PX | blocked | 1 | 1 | 7 | A | A | fixed | Interface. DISPENSER-HOLE-F answers REACH-IN (station.zil 290-297), and engine/answers.js:33 lists it. But ANSWERED_VERBS (engine/zmenus.js:386) has no REACH-IN, and MORE has none either. Checked at HEAD (seed 1, the PX): the hole offers Examine, Look inside, More… and Put something in…, with no Reach in. The typed tester got the fingertips line (r7-typed-full#29); the click tester could not. It is the same gap on DOC-HOLE-F, ID-CHANGER-SLOT-F, THERMOS-F and the drinks (answers.js). Fix: add REACH-IN to ANSWERED_VERBS. Row: r7-click-fullB#24. |
| SF-154 | Round 7 vocabulary: "writing" (the Forms Storage boxes) and "printing" (the Printing Plant; Station Control's PRINTING) | Parser / Printing Plant | parse | 3 | 3 | 7 | A | A | fixed | D28 item 6, the standing rule. Oracle, seed 1: AFT, READ WRITING gives [I don't know the word "writing."], and EXAMINE PRINTING gives [I don't know the word "printing."]. Both are printed: "Each box has some writing stamped on the side." (ship.zil 183); the room name "Printing Plant"; "PRINTING" on the system monitors (station.zil 540-575). Add WRITING as a synonym of the boxes. Add PRINTING as a room word (GLOBAL-ROOM) in the Printing Plant, as QUARTERS was added (SF-054). Rows: r7-typed-full#16, #20, #26. |
| SF-155 | The explosive's "(Out here in the cold, it has stopped softening.)" is read as a reset, but its melt is cumulative across trips | Village / Grimy Passage | blocked | 1 | 1 | 7 | A | A | fixed | Our own words (SF-113's line, rules/villageB.js:259). MELT-COUNTER only ever rises: I-EXPLOSIVE-MELT adds C-ELAPSED, or a quarter of it when the explosive is sealed in the Thermos (interrupts.zil 358-365), and no routine lowers it. The tester carried it out once, put it back, read "stopped softening" as "safe/reset", and lost it on the second trip; all three saves came after the first carry. SF-111 is the precedent: our line misread, fixed as A. Fix: "(Out here in the cold, it has stopped softening, though it has not hardened again.)" This gives no count, as SF-084 decided. Row: r7-click-fullA#21. |
| SF-156 | The D28 boots warning says "(Take them again to go ahead.)", and WEAR BOOTS then scrambles the card at once | Village / Junk Yard | blocked | 1 | 1 | 7 | A | A | fixed | Our own words (rules/library.js:1338, SF-112). Transcript: command 292 TAKE BOOTS gives the warning with "(Take them again to go ahead.)"; command 293 WEAR BOOTS gives "[taking the pair of magnetic boots first]" and the scramble. That is D28 (1) and (5) as specified: one warning, and WEAR's take counts as the repeat. But the tail names only Take. Fix: "(Taking or wearing them again goes ahead.)", and the same on the WEAR-first line. It stays one warning. Row: r7-typed-full#6. |
| SF-157 | Diagnose shows "hungry, worse in ~1 move" unchanged for about five actions, then death | Page / Pet Store | confusing | 1 | 1 | 7 | B | A | fixed | Our own D12 note (engine/zmenus.js:578-594). movesLeft floors at 1 and divides by 22 millichrons (a walk), while most actions cost 7, so "~1 move" holds for up to six actions. At HUNGER-LEVEL 4 the next tick is death (globals.zil 1214-1219), which "worse" understates. Fix: count in the time the next actions will cost, and at the last stage say "collapse" rather than "worse". Row: r7-click-fullB#23. |
| SF-158 | "Inventory (hands full)" is read as "can take no more", yet takes still work | Page / Armory | confusing | 1 | 1 | 7 | B | A | fixed | Our own D12 label (engine/zmenus.js:575, parser.js:637). It marks eight or more things in hand, the point where a take may fumble (ITAKE and CCOUNT, verbs.zil 2552-2556, 2633). It is not a refusal: the refusal is WEIGHT over 100 (verbs.zil 2546-2549). The tester dropped the nectar needlessly. Fix: word the mark as what it means, e.g. "(a take may fumble)". Blind to: the tester's hand count at turn 423 (no inventory record at that step). Row: r7-click-fullB#12. |
| SF-159 | Harness: the tester cannot zoom a package paper, and misread the course chart on QX-17-T | Harness / Spacetruck | blocked | 1 | 1 | 7 | A | A | fixed | Harness only. showPaper (scripts/playtest.mjs:135-141) hands the tester the whole 2100×3300 scan (design/papers/FORM1-QX-17-T.png). The page can be pinch-zoomed (index.html viewport has no user-scalable=no), so a tablet player can zoom where the tester could not. The wrong course (TYPE 469) and the flight to empty space are the original (the course chart is the feelie). Fix: `--paper <id> --zoom <region>` prints a crop at full resolution. Blind to: whether the tester's row really was misread (I did not re-read the chart for that start time). Row: r7-click-fullA#35. |
| SF-160 | The spray can holds 12 puffs with no count; empty short of the Chapel, the game can no longer be won, and nothing says so | Village / Chapel | blocked | 3 | 3 | 7 | A | B | open | The original: SPRAY-COUNTER starts at 12 (village.zil 1535). SHAKE says "Slosh." until 0, then "The can seems to be empty."; SPRAY at 0 says NOTHING-HAPPENS (village.zil 1458-1482). Only a puff moves the creature a room (village.zil 1507-1522); the cage and the flame move it otherwise (village.zil 384-392; station.zil 1628-1631). The star (the M-series diode's only place, station.zil 1533-1534) needs HANGING-IN-AIR from the leash (station.zil 1496-1511). The detonator fires only with DIODE-M, because the J-series burns out (interrupts.zil 396-406). So an empty can with the creature short of the Chapel is a silent dead end, which the D28 backstop (rules/library.js:2884-2887) does not cover. The route spends 9 of 12 (route-seed1 steps 183-202). Blind to: an end-to-end oracle replay of the empty-can state (argued from the code). **For the sponsor, below.** Rows: r7-click-fullA#33, #39, r7-click-fullB#38. |
| SF-161 | Day 3: every known food is gone or deadly, and the run starves | Survival / Comm Center | blocked | 4 | 4 | 7 | A | C | left | The original. The FDU always sprays acid (station.zil 1700-1722); the coffee is poisoned (station.zil 1760-1766). The foods are the soup, the two goos (ship.zil 1338, 1380, 1389), the taffy (village.zil 354) and the nectar (village.zil 907). A meal resets the hunger clock to 2250 (V-EAT, verbs.zil 686-691), and hunger kills at level 5 (globals.zil 1194-1219). A nectar drunk without being taken never gets TOUCHBIT, so the counter yields it again (globals.zil 365-371; EAT takes nothing, syntax.zil 205). Our engine does the same (r7-typed-full commands 537 and 872). The route wins on three meals. Kept. Rows: r7-typed-full#22, #24, r7-click-fullB#18, #22. |
| SF-162 | Station Control reads FOOD PRODUCTION GREEN on day 3 while the FDUs spray acid | Station / Station Control | confusing | 1 | 1 | 7 | B | C | left | The original: SYSTEM-MONITORS-F prints GREEN for FOOD PRODUCTION when DAY > 2 (station.zil 561-565), and FDU-F always sprays acid (station.zil 1700-1722). The machines report themselves fine. Kept. Row: r7-typed-full#25. |
| SF-163 | Tiredness is a hard clock: asleep off a bed, a welder kills; asleep in the suit, you suffocate | Survival / Saloon | tedious | 1 | 1 | 7 | B | C | left | The original: at SLEEPY-LEVEL 5 you drop where you stand (I-SLEEP-WARNINGS, globals.zil 925-944). The tester calls it "tense but fair". Kept. Row: r7-typed-full#14. |
| SF-164 | Day 3: walking into the elevator shaft is a fatal plunge, though on day 2 it was weightless | Station / Printing Plant | confusing | 1 | 1 | 7 | B | C | left | The original: on DAY > 2 the shaft has one Gee, and unless the elevator is one level below it is "a long plunge" (station.zil 2950-2968). This is a fast, informed death, D28 (4). Kept. Row: r7-typed-full#17. |

Both lives restored the save made at command 881. In the first, the player slept (transcript command 1122: "NOVEM 7" wake) and died on day 4; in the second they did not sleep and died on day 3. Kept. Row: r7-typed-full#27. |
| SF-166 | Launching with the spacetruck hatch open kills you, and once seated you cannot reach the hatch | Duffy / Spacetruck | other | 2 | 2 | 7 | C | C | left | The original: "Once in space, the truck's air gushes out through the open hatch." (ship.zil 1166). Both testers undid it or restarted and call it fair. Kept. Rows: r7-typed-full#28, r7-click-fullA#2. |

| SF-168 | The platinum detector is "too hot to pick up" with Floyd far away, and was blamed on the junk pile | Village / Alley | confusing | 1 | 1 | 7 | B | C | left | The original: the heat is time switched on, not nearness. DETECTOR-COUNTER rises each turn it is on; it gets warm at 50 and 75 and is dropped at 100 (interrupts.zil 64-82). TAKE refuses above 99 (village.zil 1053-1056), and OFF resets it (village.zil 1049-1051). Kept. Row: r7-click-fullA#24. |

Row: r7-click-fullA#28. |

Kept. Row: r7-click-fullA#29. |

The two keypads are different things, and each thing keeps its own number (SF-043). Restore's entries are the saves of that moment, which change as saves rotate. Kept. Kept. Row: r7-click-fullA#36. |
| SF-174 | Search on the Pawn Shop ceiling: "You can't search a ceiling!" (read as a hint, after the letter's "ceiling panel") | Click menus / Pawn Shop | confusing | 1 | 1 | 7 | B | C | left | The original's reply: oracle, route step 159 + SEARCH CEILING: "You can't search a ceiling!". The neck refusal is canon too, and the coffee is poisoned (station.zil 1760-1766). Kept. Row: r7-click-fullB#28. |
| SF-177 | The drunk ostrich's menu offers "Get in" and "Sit in" | Click menus / "Doc" Schuster's | confusing | 1 | 1 | 7 | B | C | left | The original: OSTRICH-F answers ENTER and CLIMB-ON with its scare (village.zil 1747-1748). In the PX, that scare is what frees the timer (village.zil 1753-1756). The entries come from the routine's answers. Kept. Row: r7-click-fullB#30. |

| SF-011 | The Greasy Straw counter's menu offers Open ("You have lost your mind"), then Search says to open it first | Click menus / Greasy Straw | confusing | 2 | 4 | 1, 7 | B | A | fixed | Round 7: 2 more (r7-click-fullA#18, r7-click-fullB#17).
